mainTopic: The כהן גדול's Torah reading on יום כיפור, and the king's reading at הקהל
overview: This amud finishes the כהן גדול's Torah reading on יום כיפור and then begins the king's reading at הקהל. רב חסדא first explains that the reading took place in the עזרת נשים. The גמרא then asks how the כהן גדול may skip from 'אחרי מות' to 'אך בעשור', since a משנה says you may not skip in the Torah. אביי's final answer is that skipping is allowed within one topic, and a ברייתא backs him up with more rules about skipping. Next, the גמרא explains why the כהן גדול says the במדבר section by heart: we do not roll a scroll while the ציבור waits, and we do not bring a second scroll, because people might think the first is flawed or because it would mean an unnecessary ברכה. A ברייתא then lists his eight ברכות. A new משנה describes הקהל: when it happens, how the scroll is handed up to the king, the story of אגריפס, what the king reads, and his ברכות. The גמרא fixes 'בשמיני' to mean the eighth year, then begins explaining why the פסוק needs each of its time words, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse that ends the challenge about where the reading took place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא with a verse from נחמיה. That ברייתא seems to place the Torah reading somewhere other than the עזרת נשים named in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he read from it before the open square that was in front of the Water Gate"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge it began just before this point. It quotes the last line of a ברייתא, a verse, which seems to disagree with the משנה about where the כהן גדול read the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the reading happened in the עזרת נשים. The ברייתא, which ends with this verse about עזרא reading publicly, gives a different location. The exclamation mark shows this is the end of a challenge that still needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: An open square or wide public space
The Water Gate, one of the gates of ירושלים
And he read (here, עזרא reading the Torah to the people)

phrases.english: "And he read from it before the broad place
phrases.notes: נחמיה 8:3. This verse is the last line of the ברייתא the גמרא quoted just before, to challenge the משנה.

phrases.english: that was in front of the Water Gate"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּקְרָא בוֹ לִפְנֵי הָרְחוֹב אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי שַׁעַר הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a contradiction that began before this section of the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the כהן גדול reads in the עזרת נשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, backed by this verse, seems to place the reading somewhere else, so the location in the משנה seems contradicted.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא also means the women's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction. When the ברייתא names a courtyard, it means the עזרת נשים, just like the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It means in the women's courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge. He reads the ברייתא so that it agrees with the משנה: the reading took place in the עזרת נשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real disagreement. The ברייתא's wording is simply explained as referring to the same place the משנה names. This closes the question about where the reading happened.

keyTerms.meaning: The women's courtyard, the outer courtyard of the בית המקדש
An אמורא who answers the challenge here

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's Torah reading on יום כיפור took place in the עזרת נשים, and רב חסדא reads the ברייתא to match that.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
In the women's courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's location so it matches the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to place the reading somewhere other than the עזרת נשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא also means the עזרת נשים, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the כהן גדול reads two separate sections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. The כהן גדול reads the section 'אחרי מות' and the section 'אך בעשור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he reads "After the death" and "But on the tenth."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This line sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two sections are both in ספר ויקרא, but they are not next to each other; other sections come in between. So reading both means skipping from one place in the Torah scroll to another. The next step challenges exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about the יום כיפור service
The Torah section about the day of יום כיפור among the holidays

phrases.english: And he reads "After the death"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:1

phrases.english: and "But on the tenth."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:26. It is not right after the first section, so he has to skip ahead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה after the location question was settled
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול reads both 'אחרי מות' and 'אך בעשור', which means skipping between them.

steps.title: A contradiction: skipping in the Torah is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that allows skipping in נביא but forbids skipping in the Torah. That seems to contradict the כהן גדול skipping from 'אחרי מות' to 'אך בעשור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they pointed out a contradiction: One may skip around when reading from the Prophets, but one may not skip around when reading from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה with another משנה. That source says you may not skip around in the Torah, yet the כהן גדול does exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה has the כהן גדול jumping from one section to a later one. The משנה in מגילה says skipping is allowed only in נביא, not in the Torah. The two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction (one source is set against another)
They skip, meaning jumping from one passage to another during the reading
The Prophets, as in the reading of the הפטרה

phrases.english: And they pointed out a contradiction:
One may skip around in the Prophets
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מגילה 24a.

phrases.english: but one may not skip around in the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: ורְמִינְהִי: מְדַלְּגִין בְּנָבִיא וְאֵין מְדַלְּגִין בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the משנה quoted in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The כהן גדול skipping from 'אחרי מות' to 'אך בעשור'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in מגילה forbids skipping in the Torah, but our משנה has the כהן גדול skip in the Torah.

steps.title: אביי: a short skip is allowed, a long skip is not
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the rule depends on the length of the skip. Skipping is forbidden if it takes so long that the תורגמן finishes and is left waiting. It is allowed if the skip is short enough that he does not finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is not difficult. One case is where the skip takes long enough that the translator finishes and stops. The other case is where it is short enough that the translator does not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. Each source is talking about a different length of skip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the Torah was read, a תורגמן translated each verse aloud into Aramaic. The משנה in מגילה forbids a long skip, where the congregation would be left waiting in silence. Our משנה allows the כהן גדול's skip because it is short enough that the תורגמן is still translating when the reading continues.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
The translator who recited the Aramaic translation of the reading aloud
Will stop or finish
An אמורא who gives the answer here

steps.confusionAlert: Which כאן is which? The first כאן (the translator stops, a long skip) is the משנה in מגילה, where skipping is forbidden. The second כאן (the translator does not stop, a short skip) is our משנה, where skipping is allowed.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
Here, where the skip is long enough that the translator finishes,
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה in מגילה, where skipping is forbidden.

phrases.english: here, where it is short enough that the translator does not finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into two different cases (a long skip versus a short skip)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Skipping in the Torah seemed to be forbidden completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a long skip, where the תורגמן would finish and wait, is forbidden. A short skip, like the כהן גדול's, is allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that the translator rule applies only to נביא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי with a ברייתא. It applies the 'translator does not finish' limit only to skipping in נביא, which implies that in the Torah you may not skip at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught about this very rule: One may skip in the Prophets but not in the Torah. And how far may one skip? Only as far as the translator will not finish. This implies that in the Torah one may not skip at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer. A ברייתא uses the translator limit only for נביא, so it seems the Torah has no such allowance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי used the translator limit to permit short skips in the Torah. But the ברייתא gives that limit as the measure for skipping in נביא, right after saying 'not in the Torah'. So the inference is that skipping in the Torah is never allowed, even a short skip, and our משנה is difficult again.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught about this very rule? (introduces a source that challenges an answer)
And up to how much? (asks for a measurement)
By implication; we can infer from this
Not at all, in no amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks down אביי's first answer. In step 7 he gives a new way to explain how the כהן גדול may skip in the Torah.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught about it:
One may skip in the Prophets
but one may not skip in the Torah.
And how far may one skip?
As long as the translator does not finish.
This implies that in the Torah
one may not skip at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a short skip is allowed in the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the translator limit only for נביא, which implies that the Torah allows no skipping at all, not even a short skip.

steps.title: אביי's new answer: one topic versus two topics
steps.stepSummary: אביי drops his first answer and gives a new one. Skipping in the תורה is allowed within one topic, but not between two different topics.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: there is no contradiction. Our משנה is talking about skipping within one topic. The other משנה is talking about skipping between two topics.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a brand-new answer to the contradiction from Step 4, because his first answer was knocked down in Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer does not depend on how long the skip takes. It depends on the subject matter. 'אחרי מות' and 'אך בעשור' are both about יום כיפור, so the כהן גדול may skip between them. The משנה that forbids skipping in the תורה means skipping between two unrelated topics.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction.
One topic or subject.
Two different topics.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: it is not difficult.
Here, it is within one topic;
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה about the כהן גדול. Both of his sections are about יום כיפור.

phrases.english: there, it is between two topics.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה from Step 4 that forbids skipping in the תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer from Step 5, which was knocked down in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): one topic versus two topics
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on skipping in the תורה applies to every skip, so the כהן גדול's skip should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Skipping in the תורה is allowed within a single topic. The ban applies only to skipping between different topics.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the one-topic rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing. In the תורה you may skip within one topic, and in נביא you may skip even between two topics. In both cases the skip must be short enough that the תורגמן does not finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was taught in a ברייתא: one may skip in the תורה within one topic, and in נביא even between two topics. In both cases, only if the skip is short enough that the translator does not finish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up אביי's new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states exactly אביי's split: one topic in the תורה, two topics in נביא. It also keeps the 'translator does not finish' limit for both. So the time limit is still true, but it was not enough on its own to answer the question.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (in a ברייתא). Here it brings support, not a challenge.
One may skip from one passage to another.
The translator who translated the reading into Aramaic for the listeners.
Will stop or finish.

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'וְהָתַנְיָא' often opens a challenge. Here it does the opposite: it means 'and so it was taught' and supports אביי.

phrases.english: And so it was taught in a ברייתא:
One may skip in the Torah within one topic,
and in the Prophets even between two topics.
And in both cases,
only as far as the translator will not finish in the meantime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split between one topic and two topics
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows skipping in the תורה within one topic and in נביא across two topics

steps.title: More skipping rules for the books of the Prophets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. You may not skip from one book of נביאים to another. Within תרי עשר you may skip, but not backward from the end of the book to its beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not skip from one book of the Prophets to another. But among the Twelve Prophets one may skip, as long as he does not skip from the end of the book back to its beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא keeps going and adds rules about skipping between books of נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skipping inside one book of נביא is fine, but jumping to a different book is not. תרי עשר is treated as one book, so moving between its prophets is allowed. However, you must go forward in the order they are written, not backward.

keyTerms.meaning: From one book of the Prophets to another.
The Twelve (minor) Prophets, written together as one book.
Provided that; only on condition that.

steps.whatToRemember: תורה: you may skip only within one topic. נביא: you may skip even between topics, but not to another book. תרי עשר: you may skip, but only forward. In every case, the skip must be short enough that the translator does not finish.

phrases.english: And one may not skip from one prophet to another prophet.
But among the prophets of the Twelve, one may skip,
provided that he does not skip
from the end of the book back to its beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more rules about skipping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No skipping between books of נביאים. Within תרי עשר skipping is allowed, but only forward.

steps.title: The משנה: the כהן גדול rolls up the Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. The כהן גדול rolls up the ספר תורה and places it in his lap.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and he rolls up the Torah scroll and places it in his lap, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a short question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After reading 'אחרי מות' and 'אך בעשור' from the scroll, the כהן גדול rolls it up. The משנה goes on to say that he announces more is written there than what he read. He then recites the last section by heart.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolls up (a scroll).
His lap or bosom.
Etc. It means the quoted line continues.

phrases.english: And he rolls up the Torah scroll
and places it in his lap, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the line: he says, 'More than what I read before you is written here.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the skipping discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול rolls up the scroll, holds it, and announces that more is written there than he read.

steps.title: Why does he need to say all this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the כהן גדול has to announce that more is written in the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all of this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the כהן גדול's announcement. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a public statement while holding the scroll seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what it accomplishes.

keyTerms.meaning: And why all of this?

phrases.english: And why all of this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה quoted in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the כהן גדול's announcement that more is written in the scroll.

steps.title: So people will not think badly of the Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: He says it so that people will not cast doubt on the ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So as not to cast a bad name on the Torah scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The announcement protects the honor of the ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול reads the last section by heart instead of from the scroll. People might think that section is missing from the scroll. His announcement makes clear that it is written there too.

keyTerms.meaning: To spread a bad name or cast doubt.

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול announces that more is written in the scroll only to protect the honor of the ספר תורה. That way no one thinks the part he says by heart is missing from it.

phrases.english: so as not to cast a bad name
on the Torah scroll.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The announcement prevents people from thinking the section he says by heart is missing from the ספר תורה.

steps.title: The משנה: the third reading is said by heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. The כהן גדול recites the portion of ובעשור from ספר במדבר by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the portion 'And on the tenth' in the book of Numbers, he reads by heart."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier portions were read from the scroll. This one is in a different book, so the כהן גדול recites it from memory. The next step asks why he does not just read it from the scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for ספר במדבר, the book of Numbers
By heart, from memory
"And on the tenth", the opening words of the יום כיפור offerings portion

phrases.english: "And on the tenth" in the book of Numbers
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:7

phrases.english: he reads by heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶעָשׂוֹר שֶׁבְּחוֹמֶשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים קוֹרֵא עַל פֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה after the discussion of the כהן גדול's announcement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול recites the במדבר portion of יום כיפור from memory.

steps.title: Why not roll the scroll to that place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the כהן גדול does not roll the ספר תורה to ובעשור and read it from the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him roll the scroll to that place and read it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why reading from memory is needed when he could just roll the scroll to the right spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading from the written scroll is the normal way. So the גמרא wants to know what stops him from rolling the scroll to במדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him roll it (the scroll)
Let him read

phrases.english: But let him roll the scroll and read!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the rule just quoted from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why recite from memory instead of rolling the scroll to the passage?

steps.title: We do not roll a Torah scroll in front of the congregation
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה in the name of רב ששת answers that a ספר תורה is not rolled in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: Because one may not roll a ספר תורה in public.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that rolling the scroll far ahead while everyone waits is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the ציבור sit and wait while the scroll is rolled to another book is not respectful to them. Reciting by heart avoids that wait.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolling a scroll
In public, in front of the congregation

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said
Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין גּוֹלְלִין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בַּצִּבּוּר.
phrases.english: Because one may not roll a Torah scroll in public.
phrases.notes: He means rolling a long way to a new spot while everyone sits and waits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ספר תורה is not rolled in front of the ציבור, out of respect for them.

steps.title: Why not bring a second scroll?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they do not bring another ספר תורה, already rolled to the right place, and read from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them bring another Torah scroll and read from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests another way around the problem: use a second scroll that is already open to ובעשור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second scroll prepared ahead of time would avoid making the ציבור wait. So רב ששת's reason alone does not explain why he must recite by heart.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them bring
Another, a different one

phrases.english: But let them bring another Torah scroll and read!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes further after רב ששת's answer, suggesting a second scroll.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why not use a second, pre-rolled scroll?

steps.title: People would think the first scroll is flawed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה answers that bringing a second scroll would make it look as if the first one has a flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said: Because of the flaw of the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה gives one reason not to bring a second scroll: people would suspect the first one is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the same reader suddenly switches scrolls, onlookers may assume a mistake was found in the first. To protect the first scroll's good name, no second scroll is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Its flaw, a blemish on its reputation
The first one (the first scroll)

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said:
Because of the flaw of the first one.
phrases.notes: Not a real flaw. He means people would think the first scroll had a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר מִשּׁוּם פְּגָמוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second scroll would make people think the first was flawed.

steps.title: A second scroll would bring an unnecessary blessing
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different answer: a second scroll would require an extra ברכה that is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Because one may not recite a blessing that is unnecessary.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers a second, different reason not to bring another scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading from a new scroll would call for a new ברכה. Since he can read the portion without it, that ברכה would be a ברכה שאינה צריכה, which is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnecessary blessing
We recite a blessing

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מְבָרְכִין בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה.
phrases.english: Because one may not recite a blessing that is unnecessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מְבָרְכִין בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to step 16, alongside רב הונא בר יהודה's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second scroll would cause an extra, unnecessary ברכה.

steps.title: Challenge: on ראש חודש טבת three scrolls are used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא בר יהודה. רבי יצחק נפחא rules that when ראש חודש טבת falls on שבת, three scrolls are brought, so the fear of a 'flaw' seems not to matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are we really concerned about a flaw? Didn't רבי יצחק נפחא say: When ראש חודש טבת falls on שבת, one brings three Torah scrolls and reads: one for the topic of the day, one for ראש חודש, and one for חנוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא בר יהודה's reason by pointing to a case where several scrolls are used without worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If using many scrolls were a problem, it should be a problem on ראש חודש טבת too. Yet there we bring three scrolls, so the worry of making people think a scroll is flawed seems to be ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned
A flaw (Aramaic)
The new month of טבת, which falls during חנוכה
The topic of the day, the regular weekly portion

phrases.english: But are we concerned about a flaw?
But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha say:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ טֵבֵת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.english: When the New Moon of Tevet falls on Shabbat
one brings three Torah scrolls and reads:
one for the topic of the day,
phrases.notes: That means the regular weekly שבת portion.

phrases.english: and one of the New Moon,
and one of Chanukah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חָיְישִׁינַן לִפְגָמָא וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב הונא בר יהודה's answer in step 17 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר יהודה's concern that a second scroll makes the first look flawed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On ראש חודש טבת that falls on שבת, three scrolls are used without any worry about a flaw. So the worry should not stop a second scroll on יום כיפור either.

steps.title: Three readers with three scrolls is different from one reader with two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when three men read from three scrolls, nobody suspects a flaw. When one man switches from one scroll to another, people do suspect a flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three men with three scrolls: there is no flaw. One man with two scrolls: there is a flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא בר יהודה by showing how the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש חודש טבת each reader gets his own scroll, which looks natural. The כהן גדול is one person, so if he switches scrolls in the middle, people will think something was wrong with the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: Men
Scrolls
There is not / there is

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול recites ובעשור by heart for two reasons. We do not make the ציבור wait while a scroll is rolled, and we do not bring a second scroll because one man switching scrolls makes the first look flawed (or, according to ריש לקיש, because it would bring an unnecessary ברכה).

phrases.english: Three men with three scrolls:
there is no flaw,
one man with two scrolls:
there is a flaw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by showing how the cases differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using several scrolls never makes people suspect a flaw, as on ראש חודש טבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one reader switching scrolls makes people suspect a flaw. Separate readers with separate scrolls do not.

steps.title: Listing the blessings the כהן גדול recites
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the eight ברכות and brings a ברייתא that lists what they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the כהן גדול recites eight blessings. The רבנן taught which ones: a blessing on the Torah like in the בית הכנסת; blessings on the עבודה, הודאה, and מחילת עון, worded as usual; and separate blessings for the מקדש, the כהנים, ישראל, and ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and uses a ברייתא to explain exactly which blessings the כהן גדול says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of these blessings are said in their normal, familiar wording, like the ones in davening. Others are special blessings, each said on its own for one topic: the מקדש, the כהנים, ישראל, and ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple service (a blessing asking ה׳ to accept it)
Thanksgiving (the 'מודים' blessing)
Forgiveness of sin
In their set, established wording
On its own, as a separate blessing

phrases.english: And he recites eight blessings over it, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
One recites a blessing over the Torah
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: the way one blesses in the synagogue,
and over the Temple service, and over thanksgiving,
and over forgiveness of sin, in their set form.
over the Temple on its own,
and over the priests on their own,
over Israel on their own,
and over Jerusalem on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of a second scroll and moves on to explain the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכות are: Torah, עבודה, הודאה, and מחילת עון in their usual wording, plus separate blessings for the מקדש, כהנים, ישראל, and ירושלים.

steps.title: What 'the rest of the prayer' means
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה's phrase 'and the rest is prayer': a plea for the salvation of ישראל, ending with שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'and the rest is prayer.' The Rabbis taught: the rest is a prayer, a plea, a song, and a request, that Your people ישראל need to be saved. He ends with 'Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that tells us what this last prayer contains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The rest is prayer' is vague in the משנה. The ברייתא fills it in. It is a heartfelt request for the salvation of ישראל, and it closes with the חתימה of שומע תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Plea, supplication
Song, joyful prayer
Request
Closes the blessing (the ending 'ברוך אתה ה׳...')
'Who hears prayer', the closing words of the blessing

phrases.english: And the rest is prayer.
The Rabbis taught: the rest is prayer,
supplication, song, and request
that Your people Israel need to be saved.
And he concludes with 'Who hears prayer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the list of ברכות by defining its last item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The final prayer asks for the salvation of ישראל and ends with שומע תפלה.

steps.title: Everyone reads from his own Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that after this, each person brings his own ספר תורה from home and reads from it, to show off its beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, each and every person brings a Torah scroll from his house and reads from it. Why all this? To show its beauty to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes what happens after the כהן גדול finishes. Everyone reads from his own scroll, and the ברייתא explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not because the כהן גדול's reading was missing something. People bring their own beautiful scrolls to show the crowd how much they love the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: From this point on
Its appearance, its beauty
To the public, to the many

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא explains the end of the משנה: the כהן גדול's ברכות (Torah, עבודה, הודאה, מחילה, מקדש, כהנים, ישראל, ירושלים, and a closing prayer ending שומע תפלה). Afterward everyone shows off his own ספר תורה.

phrases.english: From here on,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵבִיא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: each and every person brings a Torah scroll
from his home and reads from it.
And why all this?
In order to show its beauty to the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵבִיא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, describing what happens after the כהן גדול's ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Afterward, each person reads from his own ספר תורה to display its beauty publicly.

steps.title: When and where the king reads at הקהל
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: the king's reading takes place after the first day of סוכות in the year after שמיטה, on a wooden platform in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How is the king's portion done? After the first day of the festival of סוכות, in the eighth year, right after שמיטה, they make him a wooden platform in the Temple courtyard, and he sits on it. As the פסוק says: 'At the end of seven years, at the set time...'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains the king's Torah reading at הקהל: when it happens and where the king sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing comes from the פסוק about הקהל, which speaks of 'the end of seven years.' So the reading happens in the year right after שמיטה, during סוכות. A special wooden platform is built for the king in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The king's Torah reading at הקהל
The seventh year, שמיטה
A raised platform
The Temple courtyard
Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'

phrases.english: Mishnah:
How is the king's portion read?

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג,
phrases.english: At the end of the first festival day of the Festival,
phrases.notes: 'The Festival' here means סוכות.

phrases.english: in the eighth, at the end of the seventh year,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשִׂין לוֹ בִּימָה שֶׁל עֵץ בָּעֲזָרָה
phrases.english: they make for him a wooden platform in the courtyard
and he sits on it,
as it is stated: 'At the end of seven years, at the set time, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 31:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: the king's reading instead of the כהן גדול's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king reads at הקהל, after the first day of סוכות in the year after שמיטה, sitting on a wooden platform in the עזרה.

steps.title: The scroll is handed up to the king
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the ספר תורה passes from the חזן up through the officials to the king, who stands to receive it and sits to read.
steps.simpleTranslation: The synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll and gives it to the head of the synagogue. The head of the synagogue gives it to the סגן, the סגן gives it to the כהן גדול, and the כהן גדול gives it to the king. The king stands and receives it, and reads sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the ceremony of passing the scroll up, step by step, from the lowest official to the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll passes up a chain of officials, each handing it to someone of higher rank, until it reaches the king. The king stands when he receives it, but he reads while sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: The synagogue attendant
The head of the synagogue
The deputy of the כהן גדול
The High Priest

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier case. There the כהן גדול was the reader. Here the כהן גדול only hands the scroll to the king, and the king is the one who reads.

phrases.english: The synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll
and gives it to the head of the synagogue,
and the head of the synagogue gives it to the deputy,
and the deputy gives it to the High Priest,
and the High Priest gives it to the king.
And the king stands and receives it,
and reads sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹטֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְנוֹתְנָהּ לְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from the setting to the handing over of the scroll.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scroll passes חזן → ראש הכנסת → סגן → כהן גדול → king. The king stands to receive it and reads sitting.
steps.whyThisMatters: The detail that the king reads sitting sets up the discussion that follows in the גמרא.

steps.title: King Agrippa reads standing and weeps at the verse about a foreign king
steps.stepSummary: אגריפס המלך stood for the whole reading and was praised. When he reached the פסוק forbidding a foreign king, he cried, and the people reassured him that he is their brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: King אגריפס stood up, received the ספר תורה, and read it standing, and the חכמים praised him. When he reached 'You may not appoint a foreigner over you,' tears ran from his eyes. They said to him: Don't be afraid, אגריפס, you are our brother, you are our brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story about a real king, אגריפס, who chose to stand for the whole reading even though a king is allowed to sit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the king stands to receive the ספר תורה and sits to read. אגריפס went further and read standing, which earned praise. His tears at the פסוק about a foreign king, and the people's answer, show how worried he was about his own right to be king.

keyTerms.meaning: King Agrippa, a king of ישראל in the time of the second בית המקדש
they praised him
a foreigner, someone not from among the Jewish people
his eyes flowed with tears
you are our brother

phrases.english: King Agrippa stood up and received [the scroll]
and read while standing,
and the Sages praised him.
And when he reached "You may not
appoint a foreigner over you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 17:15

phrases.english: tears flowed from his eyes.
They said to him: Do not be afraid, Agrippa,
you are our brother, you are our brother!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרִיפַּס הַמֶּלֶךְ עָמַד וְקִבֵּל וְקָרָא עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example right after the rule that the king stands to receive the scroll and sits to read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אגריפס read standing and was praised; when he cried at the foreign-king פסוק, the people told him he was their brother.

steps.title: Which sections of ספר דברים the king reads
steps.stepSummary: The king reads from the start of דברים until שמע, then specific sections: שמע, והיה אם שמוע, the tithe sections, the section about the king, and the blessings and curses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king reads from the beginning of 'These are the words' until 'Hear O Israel', and then 'Hear O Israel', 'And it shall be if you listen', 'You shall surely tithe', 'When you finish tithing', the section about the king, and the blessings and curses, until he finishes the whole section.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists exactly which parts of the תורה the king reads at הקהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he reads straight through from the very start of ספר דברים until שמע ישראל. After that he does not read everything, only chosen sections: the two parts of שמע, the two tithe sections, the king's section, and the blessings and curses.

keyTerms.meaning: the opening words of ספר דברים
the section about tithes (מעשרות)
the section about finishing the tithes (וידוי מעשר)
the section of laws about the king
the blessings and curses of the תורה

phrases.english: And he reads from the beginning of "These are the words,"
phrases.notes: דברים 1:1

phrases.english: until "Hear," and then "Hear,"
phrases.notes: He reads straight through up to שמע ישראל, and then reads the שמע section itself.

phrases.english: "And it shall be, if you listen,"
"You shall surely tithe,"
"When you finish tithing,"
and the section about the king,
and the blessings and curses,
until he finishes the entire section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing how the king gets the scroll, the משנה now says what he reads from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king reads דברים from the start until שמע, then the listed sections, through the blessings and curses.

steps.title: The king says the כהן גדול's ברכות, with one change
steps.stepSummary: The king says the same ברכות the כהן גדול says on יום כיפור, but he replaces the ברכה about forgiveness of sin with one about the festivals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברכות that the כהן גדול says, the king says too, except that he says a ברכה about the festivals instead of the one about forgiveness of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us which ברכות the king says after reading, by comparing them to the ברכות of the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving a new list, the משנה points back to the eight ברכות of the כהן גדול from earlier. Only one is swapped: forgiveness of sin fits יום כיפור, so at הקהל, held on סוכות, the king blesses about the festivals instead.

keyTerms.meaning: the High Priest
a ברכה about the festivals (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
forgiveness of sin

steps.whatToRemember: The king's reading ends with the same ברכות as the כהן גדול on יום כיפור, except a festival ברכה replaces the forgiveness ברכה.

phrases.english: The blessings that the High Priest recites
the king recites them,
except that he gives one about the Festivals
in place of the one about forgiveness of sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְבָרֵךְ אוֹתָן הַמֶּלֶךְ מְבָרֵךְ אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the reading itself, the משנה gives the ברכות said at the end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king says the כהן גדול's ברכות, swapping forgiveness of sin for a festival ברכה.

steps.title: Can 'on the eighth' really mean the eighth day of סוכות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by questioning the משנה's word 'בשמיני', since the משנה already said the reading happens after the first day of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'On the eighth' — could that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by challenging a word in the משנה that does not seem to make sense. This sets up the correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the reading is on מוצאי יום טוב הראשון של חג, then said 'בשמיני'. If that meant the eighth day of סוכות, it would contradict the first time given. So the גמרא says this reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion that explains the משנה
could it enter your mind? (a way of saying: that can't be right)
on the eighth (masculine form, sounds like the eighth day)

phrases.english: Gemara:
"On the eighth" — could that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts its discussion by going back to the opening words of this משנה (step 24).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading it as the eighth day of סוכות clashes with the משנה's own statement that the reading is after the first day of סוכות.

steps.title: Read it as 'in the eighth year'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the reading: say 'בשמינית', meaning the eighth year, the year after שמיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'in the eighth' [year].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by changing how the word is read, so it refers to the eighth year instead of the eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'בשמיני' to 'בשמינית' turns the word into a feminine form that goes with 'שנה', a year. The eighth year is the year right after the seven-year שמיטה cycle ends, which matches 'במוצאי שביעית'.

keyTerms.meaning: say instead; read it this way
in the eighth (feminine form, meaning the eighth year)

phrases.english: Rather, say: "in the eighth" [year].
phrases.notes: The feminine ending goes with the word שנה, so it means the eighth year, right after שמיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting how a word in the משנה is read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בשמיני' might seem to mean the eighth day of סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'בשמינית': the eighth year of the cycle, the year after שמיטה.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need all these time details?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק of הקהל lists so many time markers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: the פסוק about הקהל gives several time details, so why do we need every one of them? This line sets up the long answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'מקץ שבע שנים, במעד שנת השמטה, בחג הסכות.' It looks like one or two of these words should be enough to tell us when הקהל happens. The גמרא wants to show that each word teaches something the others do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking what a word or detail adds)
These (the time words in the פסוק)
The gathering of all Israel to hear the king read the תורה

phrases.english: And why do I need all these?
phrases.notes: 'All these' means the time words in דברים 31:10-11: the end of seven years, the שמיטה year, the festival, סוכות, and 'when all Israel comes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the timing as the year after שמיטה, the גמרא now looks at the פסוק's many time words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each time word in the פסוק of הקהל adds.

steps.title: 'At the end' alone could mean counting from now, so the תורה adds 'שמיטה'
steps.stepSummary: With only 'מקץ' we would count seven years from now, from when this command was said, even if that did not line up with שמיטה. So the תורה writes 'שמטה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all necessary. If the תורה had written only 'at the end,' I would have said we count from now, even though it would not fall in the שמיטה year. So the תורה wrote 'שמיטה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer: every word is needed. The first link: 'at the end of seven years' alone could be counted from the moment it was said, so the word 'שמיטה' ties the count to the שמיטה cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word 'שמיטה,' the seven-year count could start whenever the פסוק was said. Then הקהל could land in a year that has nothing to do with שמיטה. The word 'שמיטה' makes the count follow the real שמיטה cycle.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (each detail teaches something)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
From now
Happens to fall out

phrases.english: They are necessary, for if the Merciful One had written only "at the end"
I would have said: let us count from now,
phrases.notes: 'From now' means from the time the תורה said this, not from the start of a שמיטה cycle.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מִתְרְמֵי בִּשְׁמִיטָּה,
phrases.english: even though it would not happen to fall in the שמיטה year;
so the Merciful One wrote "שמיטה."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question by explaining the first word in the chain.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מקץ' alone would let us count from any starting point, so 'שמטה' ties הקהל to the שמיטה cycle.

steps.title: 'שמיטה' alone could mean the end of that year, so the תורה adds 'at the festival'
steps.stepSummary: With only 'שמיטה' we might hold הקהל at the end of the שמיטה year, so the תורה writes 'במועד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'שמיטה,' I would have said it is at the end of the שמיטה year. So the תורה wrote 'at the festival.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second link: knowing it is tied to שמיטה, we might think הקהל happens at the very end of the שמיטה year. The word 'במועד' (at the festival) corrects that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know which cycle to follow, but not which point in time. 'At the festival' tells us it happens at a festival, which pushes us to the first festival after שמיטה ends.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of the שמיטה year
At the festival

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "שמיטה,"
I would have said: at the end of the שמיטה year;
so the Merciful One wrote "at the festival."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain: the word added in the last step could itself be misread.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שמטה' alone might suggest the end of the שמיטה year, so 'במעד' places it at a festival.

steps.title: 'At the festival' alone could mean ראש השנה, so the תורה adds 'סוכות'
steps.stepSummary: With only 'במועד' we might hold הקהל at the start of the year (ראש השנה), so the תורה writes 'בחג הסוכות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had written only 'at the festival,' I would have said from the start of the year. So the תורה wrote 'on the festival of סוכות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The next link: 'at the festival' could mean ראש השנה, the very start of the new year. So the תורה names the exact festival, סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word fixes the mistake the previous word left open. Now we know הקהל is on סוכות, right after the שמיטה year. The next step shows that even 'בחג הסוכות' leaves a gap, since סוכות lasts several days.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of the year, meaning ראש השנה
The festival of סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: This is a צריכותא chain: מקץ → שמטה → במעד → בחג הסכות, and the next step adds בבוא כל ישראל. Each phrase blocks a wrong reading of the one before.

phrases.english: And if it had written only "at the festival,"
I would have said: from the start of the year;
so the Merciful One wrote "on the festival of סוכות."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain by explaining why 'בחג הסוכות' is needed after 'במעד'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'במעד' alone might mean ראש השנה, so 'בחג הסכות' fixes the exact time.

steps.title: Why the Torah adds 'When all Israel comes'
steps.stepSummary: With only 'בחג הסוכות' we might hold הקהל even on the last day of the חג. So the תורה writes 'בבוא כל ישראל', which points to the beginning of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had only written 'in the חג of סוכות', I would have thought it could even be the last day of the חג. So the תורה wrote 'when all ישראל comes'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last piece of its answer about the extra time markers in the פסוק of הקהל. It explains why the תורה needed the words 'בבוא כל ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בחג הסוכות' already narrows הקהל down to סוכות, but סוכות lasts many days, so the last day might also work. 'בבוא כל ישראל' means the moment the people first arrive. That points to the start of the חג, not the end. Each phrase closes a gap the earlier phrase left open, and the sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', a way of referring to ה׳ as the One who wrote the תורה
'I would have said', what we might wrongly have thought
The last day of the חג
'When all ישראל comes', the moment the people first arrive for the חג

steps.whatToRemember: Each time marker in the פסוק has its own job: 'מקץ' and 'שמטה' fix the year, 'במועד' and 'בחג הסוכות' fix the season, and 'בבוא כל ישראל' fixes the start of the חג.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בבוא כל ישראל' as just describing who comes. Here the גמרא uses it as a time marker: the moment everyone first arrives, at the beginning of the חג.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'in the festival of Sukkot'

phrases.aramaic: — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם טוֹב אַחֲרוֹן,
phrases.english: I would have said even the last day of the Festival
So the Merciful One wrote 'when all Israel comes'
phrases.notes: דברים 31:11

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בְּחַג הַסֻּכּוֹת״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern as Steps 32-34 and fills the last gap left by 'בחג הסוכות'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק of הקהל need 'בבוא כל ישראל' after already saying 'בחג הסוכות'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without it, we might hold הקהל even on the last day of סוכות. 'בבוא כל ישראל' shows it happens when the people first arrive, at the start of the חג.
